bibliographic.title: Ethical Governance of Large Language Models in Health Care: Trust, Responsibility, and Equity in Routine Use
bibliographic.citation_apa: Yang, X., & Xu, C. (2026). Ethical governance of large language models in health care: Trust, responsibility, and equity in routine use. Journal of Medical Internet Research, 28, e93470. https://doi.org/10.2196/93470

methodology.method_family: viewpoint; adoption-phase ethics analytic lens; interaction-based ethical risk framework
methodology.technology_context: LLMs embedded in routine health care communication, clinical communication, and decision-making support; not specifically conversational agents or chatbots

eligibility.decision_rationale: Viewpoint provides a conceptual framework for ethical governance of LLMs in health care, emphasizing trust, distributed responsibility, equity, contestation, and system-level oversight during routine adoption. Strong alignment with governance and regulated-domain themes, but text provided does not center conversational systems, chatbots, agents, or operational controls such as guardrails, logging, tracing, or audit tooling.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial PDF text was supplied; extracted metadata title was corrupted; full-text sections on methods, limitations, and operational recommendations may alter eligibility and appraisal.

appraisal.notes: Conceptual viewpoint rather than empirical study; sampling and data-collection criteria are not applicable. Appraisal based on visible abstract, introduction fragment, framework mention, and acknowledgments only.

cerqual.explanation: Arguments appear coherent and objectives are explicit, but provided excerpt is incomplete and the paper offers normative framing rather than primary empirical evidence on conversational governance mechanisms.

axial_codes: ethical risk during routine LLM integration
equity in interpreting and contesting LLM outputs
coding.theme: Ethical governance of LLMs in health care during routine adoption
coding.subtheme: Trust, responsibility, and equity under institutional embedding

synthesis.main_claim: Ethical risks of LLMs in health care arise through patterns of reliance, institutional embedding, and governance during routine use, requiring continuous system-level oversight beyond technical performance evaluation.
synthesis.contribution: Introduces adoption-phase ethics and an interaction-based framework organizing ethical risk around trust, distributed responsibility, and equity in LLM-enabled health care communication.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text does not detail empirical validation, implementation mechanisms, or limitations section; operational governance tools and conversational-system specifics are not substantively covered in the excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence for ethical governance principles in regulated health care LLM adoption; supplement with studies focused on conversational systems, operational controls, and post-deployment monitoring.
